messages:
talia: heads-up — billing + node health alerts for us-central1-gpu pool. multiple nodes showing nvme firmware resets and SMART reallocated sector increases around 02:12 UTC. billing flagged a small I/O retry surge too.

sre-bot: [ALERT] nvme-reset-count spike on pool-us-central1-gpu: nodes with 2-4 resets in 10m window. local-io retry rate +20%. Autonotify sent.

danny: any host logs? smartctl or dmesg snippet would help.

talia: pasted the smartctl snippet from node gnode-231:
```
SMART Attributes Data Structure revision number: 1
ID# ATTRIBUTE_NAME          FLAG     VALUE WORST THRESH TYPE      UPDATED  WHEN_FAILED RAW_VALUE
  5 Reallocated_Sector_Ct   0x0033   095   095   010    Pre-fail  Always       -       45
199 Media_Wearout_Indicator 0x0032   083   083   000    Old_age   Always       -       170
223 Unknown_Attribute        0x0012   100   100   000    Old_age   Always       -       3

Note: Reallocated count jumped from 3 -> 45 between 02:10 and 02:13 on several hosts.
```

sam: dmesg shows a couple of nvme firmware recovery messages and subsequent IO retries:
```
[12345.678901] nvme0: async link error, reset controller
[12345.679012] nvme0n1: I/O error, dev ata1
[12346.120200] nvme0: firmware recovery succeeded, but qdepth stalls observed
```

infra-oncall: cross-checked with fw-upgrade-bot logs: there was a staggered firmware push to the nvme fleet at 01:45 UTC (rollout group A). The affected nodes are in that group plus some that had an automatic reapply.

danny: could the model-cache warmup job be hammering the drives during recovery? we had a scheduled cache-pop at 02:00.

talia: yes — warmup started at 02:02 and spawned many small write+fsyncs. Combined with firmware recovery retries -> massive write amplification on affected drives.

sre-bot: [INFO] job-scheduler: model-cache-warmup triggered 220 tasks in pool-us-central1-gpu at 02:02.

sam: iostat from a hot host (02:12):
```
iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1500.0  9000.0  60000  360000   40.0    35.0   28.5   4.1    24.4   1.10  99.9
```

talia: remediation plan proposed:
 - pause model-cache warmup immediately for the pool (done)
 - cordon + drain the 6 nodes with repeated nvme resets, allow only read-only workloads
 - rollback the firmware push to previous stable image for rollout group A (pending approval)
 - apply temporary per-node io throttle (iops and write MB/s) via cgroup on warmup jobs
 - notify finance and reduce debug retention for affected nodes to limit egress/billing

infra-oncall: cordon+drain taking ~5m per node. switching drained nodes to local-ssd readonly mount fallback is in progress.

fw-upgrade-bot: [INFO] rollback job queued for rollout-group-A firmware image 2025-01-10-rc2 -> promoting stable 2024-12-08.

finance: preliminary cost estimate: retry/backoff overhead + extra network reads ~ $600 for the 2h window. will escalate if firmware rollback leads to additional I/O.

danny: good short-term. for medium-term: need a rollout safety check — if firmware triggers farm-wide reset count >1 within 30m, pause rollout and abort.

talia: agreed. post-incident TODOs:
 - add pre-rollout smoke test that simulates concurrent small fsync-heavy warmups
 - gate model-cache warmup during firmware rollouts (scheduler temporal lock)
 - add SMART delta alert if Reallocated_Sector_Ct increases >10 in 1h
 - add cost-alert for local-io retry spike >15% over baseline
 - update playbook for read-only fallback and cordon/drain steps

sam: rollback job started on 02:40 UTC for the first 10 nodes. monitoring for further resets.

sre-bot: [INFO] incident INF-5120 created by talia  priority=P2  tags=[storage,firmware,io,billing]

talia: will keep this thread updated. if the rollback stabilizes SMART & resets, we promote rollback to the rest of rollout-group-A and then schedule a safer re-roll with staged warmup-safety and throttles.

danny: also add a CI test that exercises nvme recovery path + small-write workloads to catch regressions before firmware pushes.

talia: thanks all — keeping thread pinned for 4h and will produce RCA skeleton once logs aggregated.
